summary: spec_fidelity FAILs: REQ-2 (ubiquitous 'zero human in the runtime loop') is directly contradicted by REQ-6 (default Mode A stops for human review/click-to-publish), and this contradiction is even acknowledged in the design source as '(human = final gate)' but never resolved or scoped in the behavioral spec. REQ-8 (per-rail native monetization) and REQ-10 (payout routing by funding mode) leave an unstated but load-bearing coupling ambiguous: self-funded installs cannot pass bank KYC (REQ-10's own text) so they cannot actually use the note/Substack/Zenn native-paywall rails REQ-8 lists, yet nothing in the spec says a self-funded install must skip those rails entirely. REQ-14's 'bounded rounds' is an unquantified acceptance criterion, violating EARS testability. REQ-4 has no requirement for the insufficient-research/no-viable-topic edge case. verification_readiness FAILs: REQ-7 (Mode B autonomous publish+distribute -- the actual zero-human end-state the whole feature exists to reach) has ZERO proof obligation mapped to it in the PROP table. PROP-7/REQ-16's 'bank receipt for human-funded' T3-required gate has no defined zero-human verification mechanism anywhere in the spec or verification architecture, while the design source explicitly flags bank-KYC withdrawal as 'the real wall' (Gate 3) and leaves it open -- the behavioral spec asserts it as already solved. PROP-2's no-human audit is not evaluable as PASS/FAIL against the Mode-A default because the spec never states whether the audit scope includes or excludes the Mode-A human-review/publish click. PROP-3 verifies a semantic natural-language property (no claim of having run something) via a literal keyword blocklist, which is trivially bypassed by paraphrase. PROP-5 (required fail-closed publish gate) depends on the V0.5 craft score, which is explicitly non-deterministic/agent-judged with no defined pass rubric or threshold anywhere in the spec, making PROP-5 non-repeatable as a regression test.
